newsitem.title: USA: Auto lead battery group steps up research spending.
newsitem.headline: Auto lead battery group steps up research spending.

text.p: The Advanced Lead-Acid Battery Consortium unveiled a new three-year $17.5 million research program aimed at how best to speedily recharge batteries used in new electric vehicles, a slow growing niche market.
The ALABC's role is to make lead-acid batteries more attractive for use in electric vehicles as rival metals also advance. At present electric vehicles use lead-acid batteries.
Earlier this month General Motors said it would begin using nickel metal hydride batteries in some of its new electric vehicles, EV1, instead of lead-acid because they offered better mileage.
Another car manufacturer has said it will use a lithium ion battery in its electric vehicles.
The first ALABC contract was awarded to Cominco Limited to look at the best way to charge batteries and limit overcharging.
Electric Transportation Applications, a partnership between Arizona Public Service Co, CSIRO and Hawker Energy Products, will look for ways to improve battery lifespans.
The University of Chicago's Center for Advanced Radiation Sources will look at how batteries respond to rapid charging.
ALABC is a program of the International Lead Zinc Research Organization based in North Carolina.
